criteria.text: The response finds that Nilur's indemnity for retained Pre-Closing Product Liabilities (liabilities from implants sold before closing) expires at the 12-month general survival period, i.e. on or about April 15, 2027, leaving Tipul exposed to later-surfacing implant claims.
The response locates the indemnity survival issue in the APA at Section 8.2 (its final sentence or the Section 8.2(c) claim cut-off).
The response explains why the indemnity survival cut-off matters to Tipul.
The response recommends a fix for the indemnity survival cut-off.
The response finds that the Seller Note lets Nilur transfer the Note, together with its information and inspection rights over Tipul, to any person, including a competitor, without Tipul's consent.
The response locates the unrestricted transfer issue in the Seller Note at Section 9.
The response explains why unrestricted transfer of the Seller Note matters to Tipul.
The response recommends a fix for the unrestricted transfer of the Seller Note.

The response finds that the Seller Note's Minnesota governing law and exclusive Hennepin County, Minnesota forum control disputes under the Note, splitting the deal's disputes between Minnesota and the Delaware Court of Chancery.
The response locates the governing law and forum conflict in the Seller Note at Section 10.
The response explains why the governing law and forum conflict matters to Tipul.
The response recommends a fix for the governing law and forum conflict.

The response finds that, because the Seller Note defines 'Losses' as only amounts finally determined by a court, Tipul cannot set off good-faith pending indemnity claims against Note payments without risking a payment default under the Note.
hints: finally determined by a court of competent jurisdiction

criteria.text: The response locates the 'Losses' definition issue in the Seller Note at Section 1 (definition of 'Losses') or Section 4.2.
The response explains why the narrow Note definition of 'Losses' matters to Tipul.
The response recommends a fix for the narrow Note definition of 'Losses'.
The response states that, under the APA's order of precedence, the Seller Note controls over the APA on matters concerning the indebtedness it evidences.
The response states that the APA is governed by Delaware law.
The response is a memo that presents the issues as separate items, each giving its location, why it matters, and a recommended fix.
The response includes a section or flags identifying points it could not resolve from the documents alone.
The response claims that indemnity claims for Pre-Closing Product Liabilities benefit from the 6-year Fundamental Representation survival period.
The response claims that APA Section 11.6 restricts Nilur's transfer of the Seller Note.
